battle.name: 第一次巴爾干戰爭
battle.theater: 薩洛尼卡與馬其頓戰線
battle.brief: 第一次巴爾干戰爭於1912年10月爆發，巴爾干聯盟在馬其頓與色雷斯戰線進攻鄂圖曼帝國，戰事延續至12月。聯盟由保加利亞、塞爾維亞、希臘及蒙內哥羅組成。鄂圖曼軍隊使用惠氏步槍（Winchester Model 1873），此槍於1873年正式列裝，是當時已服役的槓桿式後膛步槍。

kit.name: 惠氏步槍
kit.history: 惠氏步槍是美軍於1873年列裝的槓桿式後膛步槍，屬早期制式步兵武器；鄂圖曼軍隊亦採用此型，將其納入陸軍步槍系統。

countries: 1912年10月初，巴爾干聯盟與奧斯曼帝國在歐洲東南部形成兩大陣營。聯盟方面包括蒙特內哥羅、塞爾維亞、保加利亞與希臘；四軍分擔不同戰區，卻沒有建立統一的戰場指揮部。蒙特內哥羅負責阿爾巴尼亞北部、斯庫台與亞得里亞灣沿岸；塞軍沿科索沃及韋爾達河向莫納斯提爾推進；保軍從內夫羅科普、塞雷斯與德拉馬方向進入馬其頓及東色雷斯，並包圍亞得里亞堡；希臘軍則由塞薩洛尼基向北攻擊基爾基斯、留蒂卡與拉哈納斯。奧斯曼方面仍控制科索沃、馬其頓、阿爾巴尼亞、色雷斯和上述要塞，但野戰部隊與各要塞守軍分屬不同指揮鏈。10月8日蒙特內哥羅首先宣戰，塞爾維亞與保加利亞在9日宣戰，希臘於19日宣戰；與此同時，奧斯曼軍仍在利比亞對義大利作戰，兵力與補給早已承擔兩面壓力。這場戰爭不是一支聯軍依序推動，而是四條戰線相互競速，並在同一批鐵路、港口和城鎮爭奪補給與撤退通道。
countriesEn: In early October 1912, the Balkan League and the Ottoman Empire formed two opposing camps in southeastern Europe. The League comprised Montenegro, Serbia, Bulgaria, and Greece, each assigned a different theater, although no unified allied command was established. Montenegro operated in northern Albania, at Scutari, and along the Adriatic coast. Serbia advanced through Kosovo and the Vardar River toward Monastir. Bulgaria entered Macedonia and eastern Thrace through the Nevrokop, Serres, and Drama directions and then surrounded Adrianople. The Greek army attacked toward Kilkis, Ljutika, and Lachanas from Salonika. The Ottomans still held Kosovo, Macedonia, Albania, Thrace, and the principal fortresses, but their field army and fortress garrisons belonged to separate chains of command. Montenegro declared war on 8 October; Serbia and Bulgaria followed on the 9th, and Greece declared war on the 19th. At the same time, Ottoman forces were still fighting Italy in Libya and had to sustain pressure on two fronts. This was not a single allied advance: it was a four-front race in which the contestants competed for the same railways, ports, towns, supplies, and routes of retreat.
people: 作戰最高層並不對稱。蒙特內哥羅國王尼古拉一世親自主持動員，武奇多戰役由沃伊斯拉夫·坦科西奇率領地面部隊，後來參與斯庫台方向的塞蒙聯軍則有塞爾維亞將軍約萬·馬奇科夫。塞爾維亞王儲亞歷山德拉居前線最高軍政位置，實際統率作戰的是總參謀長拉多米爾·普特尼克；斯特帕·斯特帕諾維奇與科斯塔·米洛瓦諾維奇等將領分掌軍、師與縱隊，普特尼克在庫馬諾沃作戰前堅持先集中砲兵、待各縱隊抵達再攻。希臘由王儲康斯坦丁主持軍政，王室參謀長亞歷山德羅斯·帕普拉斯在留蒂卡受挫後去職，喬爾吉奧斯·孔多格洛斯接掌作戰；潘亞吉奧蒂斯·丹格利斯與康斯坦丁諾斯·馬扎拉基斯－阿尼安在基爾基斯方向指揮突擊，斯蒂利安諾斯·戈納塔斯參與接收塞薩洛尼基。保加利亞的重要將領包括亞森·塔塔拉諾夫與喬爾基·托多羅夫，後者在亞得里亞堡圍城初期掌握圍城部隊。奧斯曼方面，哈桑·里扎帕夏負責蒙特內哥羅與阿爾巴尼亞戰區，謝里夫帕夏則在亞得里亞堡主持長期防守。這些指揮安排顯示，聯盟各軍可以協調目標與日期，卻難以在戰場上實行單一指揮。
peopleEn: The command arrangements were not symmetrical. King Nicholas I of Montenegro personally directed the mobilization. Vojislav Tankosić led the field forces at the Battle of Vučji Do, while the Serbo-Montenegrin force directed toward Scutari included General Jovan Mačkov. Crown Prince Alexander occupied the senior political and military position in Serbia, but Radomir Putnik exercised effective operational command as Chief of the General Staff. Generals such as Stepa Stepanović and Kosta Milovanović led armies, divisions, and columns. Before Kumanovo, Putnik insisted on concentrating the artillery and waiting for the columns to arrive before attacking. In Greece, Crown Prince Constantine headed the military administration. Chief of Staff Alexandros Papoulas resigned after the repulse at Ljutika, and Georgios Kondoglos took over operational command. Panagiotis Danglis and Konstantinos Mazarakis-Ainian directed attacks in the Kilkis sector, while Stylianos Gonatas participated in the acceptance of Salonika. Bulgaria relied on commanders including Asen Tătaranov and Georgi Todorov, the latter taking charge of the siege corps at Adrianople. On the Ottoman side, Hasan Riza Pasha directed the Montenegrin and Albanian theater, while Şerif Pasha commanded the prolonged defense of Adrianople. These arrangements show that the allies could coordinate objectives and timetables more easily than they could exercise a single command on the battlefield.
kits: 四軍的裝備並未統一到可以任意共用彈藥的程度。塞爾維亞步兵主要使用Peabody-Martini M1887及改進型M1902步槍，也裝有Mannlicher M1888/90；保軍與希軍可見Mannlicher M1888/90或M1895步槍，希臘另保留部分Lebel Model 1886舊槍，奧斯曼軍則配用Mauser Model 1888與Model 1893等栓動步槍。重機槍包括Maxim型MG08，以及奧地利設計、1907至1908年定型的Schwarzlose M1907/08。砲兵主力包括75公厘Schneider-Creusot M1897野戰砲、75公厘Krupp M1907野戰砲、105公厘Krupp M1904迫擊砲，塞爾維亞另有120公厘Schneider-Creusot M1879系列迫擊砲。75公厘與120公厘炮彈分庫供應，步槍與機槍彈藥也按口徑及年份分列，後勤官不能把不同軍械的剩餘彈藥任意混用。砲兵連作戰時以數門砲組成砲組，解炮後需有前車維持射擊，備用炮彈由彈藥車輸送；多數道路依賴馬車，進入山地砲位時最後一段仍靠馱畜。前線彈藥庫通常設在步兵營後方，軍、師指揮所與砲位之間使用野戰電話聯絡，後方再以鐵路支線和車隊銜接。裝備年代不一、補充速度不均，使各軍必須沿實際道路逐段建立彈藥線，而非一次把全部火力運上前線。
kitsEn: The four armies were not equipped to the point where ammunition could be pooled indiscriminately. Serbian infantry primarily used the Peabody-Martini M1887 and improved M1902 rifles, while Mannlicher M1888/90 rifles were also in service. Bulgarian and Greek troops used Mannlicher M1888/90 or M1895 rifles, and Greece retained some older Lebel Model 1886 rifles. Ottoman forces employed bolt-action Mauser Model 1888 and Model 1893 rifles. Machine guns included the Maxim-type MG08 and the Austrian-designed Schwarzlose M1907/08. The principal artillery pieces included the 75 mm Schneider-Creusot M1897 field gun, the 75 mm Krupp M1907 field gun, the 105 mm Krupp M1904 howitzer, and, in Serbian service, the 120 mm Schneider-Creusot M1879-series howitzer. Shells for 75 mm and 120 mm weapons were stored separately, while rifle and machine-gun ammunition was divided by caliber and date; logistics officers could not mix residual stocks from different systems without regard to caliber. Batteries were formed from several guns. Once unlimbered, each gun required a limber to remain in action, while reserve rounds were carried by ammunition caissons. Most movement depended on horse-drawn wagons, with pack animals completing the final leg to mountain positions. Forward ammunition depots were normally placed behind infantry battalions, while army and division headquarters connected with gun positions by field telephone. Rail branches and wagon trains then linked those depots to the rear. Differences in the age of equipment and the speed of resupply forced the armies to build ammunition routes stage by stage along usable roads rather than deliver all their artillery ammunition to the front at once.
tactics: 最初的實際戰鬥發生在外交程序之前。10月6日至7日，蒙特內哥羅軍在武奇多把砲位布置在高地，以步砲射擊迫使奧軍前出；奧軍騎兵的反擊未能突破陣地，隨後步兵進攻又在蒙軍火力和側翼壓迫下失去陣地。蒙特內哥羅由此取得通往亞得里亞灣的橋頭堡。塞軍主力沿庫帕奧尼克山南麓及庫馬諾沃道路推進，普特尼克先以75公厘砲逐段壓制奧軍陣地，再令步兵在砲火掩護下奪取陣地正面；庫馬諾沃于10月24日陷落，殘余守軍北撤，塞軍隨後進入斯科普里，並以另一支軍隊處理舒姆尼克。希軍初攻留蒂卡時以正面進攻爲主，遭到守軍擊退；重新集中炮兵、縮小每次攻擊目標後，部隊于16日突破奧軍陣地，繼而奪取基爾基斯，切斷通向塞薩洛尼基的道路與電報線。保軍從多個山口越過馬其頓東部防線，向塞雷斯和德拉馬推進，並與希軍戰線接近，同時把主要攻城力量轉向亞得里亞堡。該城外圍沒有被強攻，圍城部隊依靠野戰電話協調炮位和補給，守軍則利用既成工事與城內炮兵持續反擊。塞軍繼續南下取得普里茲倫，保軍與塞軍又同時進入莫納斯提爾，聯盟內部圍繞接管順序的摩擦由此時開始顯露。奧斯曼野戰部隊雖在若干會戰中潰散，殘余守軍卻能固守孤立要塞，使戰爭末段出現戰線以外的單獨圍攻。
tacticsEn: The first actual fighting occurred before the diplomatic formalities were completed. On 6 and 7 October, the Montenegrins placed guns on high ground at Vučji Do and used field artillery to force the Ottoman troops forward. An Ottoman cavalry counterattack failed to break through, and the subsequent infantry attack lost its positions under Montenegrin fire and pressure from the flanks. Montenegro thereby gained a bridgehead toward the Adriatic. The main Serbian force advanced along the southern foot of Kopaonik and the road to Kumanovo. Putnik first used 75 mm guns to suppress Ottoman positions section by section, then ordered infantry forward under covering fire to capture the fronts of their positions. Kumanovo fell on 24 October, the surviving defenders withdrew north, and the Serbs entered Skopje while another formation dealt with Šumnik. The initial Greek attack at Ljutika relied too heavily on frontal movement and was repulsed. After concentrating the artillery and limiting the objective of each attack, the Greeks broke through on 16 October, seized Kilkis, and cut the road and telegraph line toward Salonika. Bulgarian columns crossed the eastern Macedonian frontier through several passes, advanced toward Serres and Drama, came close to the Greek front, and then turned their main siege strength toward Adrianople. The city was not stormed. The besiegers coordinated guns and supplies by field telephone, while the garrison used existing fortifications and urban artillery for continuous counterfire. The Serbs continued south to seize Prizren, and Serbian and Bulgarian troops entered Monastir at nearly the same time, revealing friction over the order of occupation. Ottoman field formations disintegrated in several pitched battles, yet isolated garrisons could still hold fortified places, producing separate sieges beyond the main front as the war approached its end.
data: 可核對的戰役日程顯示，這場戰爭從正式宣戰到停戰約歷八週，但作戰起點稍早於外交日期。10月6日至7日為武奇多戰役；8日蒙特內哥羅宣戰，塞爾維亞與保加利亞次日宣戰；希臘在19日宣戰。9日至16日是留蒂卡戰役，19日至24日是庫馬諾沃戰役；同月21日希軍奪取基爾基斯，23日保軍進入內夫羅科普，24日至27日舒姆尼克守軍投降，26日塞軍占領斯科普里。11月1日拉哈納斯落入希軍手中，奧斯曼當局於2日撤出塞薩洛尼基，希軍在8日正式進城；塞軍於3日占領普里茲倫。保軍自9日起圍困亞得里亞堡，塞軍與保軍在19日進取莫納斯提爾。12月3日各方達成停戰，戰鬥至此正式停止；亞得里亞堡守軍於13日向保軍投降，斯庫台守軍也在13日投降，19日開始撤離，至20日完成 garrison 移交與城市交割。傷亡方面，各國早期公報多只統計部分會戰，奧斯曼方面的完整名冊尤其難以核對，殺傷、被俘與後送傷患的分類亦不一致，因此沒有可靠的單一總傷亡數可以引用。上述日期能顯示進攻節奏，不能用來反推各戰役的確切兵力或損失。
dataEn: The verifiable chronology shows that the war lasted about eight weeks from the formal declarations to the armistice, although combat began slightly earlier. The Battle of Vučji Do took place on 6 and 7 October. Montenegro declared war on the 8th, Serbia and Bulgaria followed on the 9th, and Greece declared war on the 19th. The Battle of Ljutika ran from 9 to 16 October, and the Battle of Kumanovo from 20 to 24 October. Greek troops seized Kilkis on 21 October; Bulgarian troops entered Nevrokop on the 23rd; the garrison at Šumnik surrendered between 24 and 27 October; and the Serbs occupied Skopje on the 26th. Lachanas fell to the Greeks on 1 November. The Ottoman authorities evacuated Salonika on the 2nd, and Greek troops formally entered the city on the 8th, while Serbian troops occupied Prizren on the 3rd. The Bulgarians began the siege of Adrianople on 9 November, and Serbian and Bulgarian forces took Monastir on the 19th. An armistice was reached on 3 December, formally ending combat. The Adrianople garrison surrendered to the Bulgarians on the 13th, as did the Scutari garrison. The latter began withdrawing on the 19th and completed the transfer of the garrison and city on the 20th. Casualty totals cannot be stated reliably: early national reports covered only selected battles, Ottoman records were particularly incomplete, and definitions of killed, captured, and evacuated wounded differed. The dates above establish the rhythm of the campaigns but cannot be used to derive exact strengths or losses for individual battles.
cause: 戰爭由數層因素同時推動。奧斯曼帝國在歐洲仍握有廣大屬地，但科索沃、阿爾巴尼亞及馬其頓的武裝起義迫使它把正規軍、砲兵與後勤單位投入內陸；同時，意土戰爭已迫使奧軍從利比亞撤退，雖未解除正式戰爭狀態，卻顯示帝國無法再把全歐軍力集中於一處。塞爾維亞希望取得科索沃與韋爾達河流域的統治權並打開通往亞得里亞海的出口，保加利亞的目標包括馬其頓、塞薩洛尼基方向及東色雷斯，希臘要求南馬其頓，並把阿埃皮魯斯、克里特與色雷斯列入長期目標，蒙特內哥羅則集中於斯庫台及阿爾巴尼亞北部。這些目標互相重疊，卻沒有共同界線方案。塞爾維亞與保加利亞於3月13日簽訂秘密同盟條約，希臘在5月29日加入軍事安排；各國雖能協調動員日期，卻各自保留軍隊與戰區。直接引爆點是蒙特內哥羅在10月初提出的最後通牒，其內容涉及阿爾巴尼亞境內奧軍、斯庫台防務與奧方拒絕接受蒙方要求。蒙軍先行進攻後，蒙特內哥羅於8日正式宣戰，其餘盟國隨即依計畫投入攻勢，因此外交危機很快轉成四條戰線同時展開的戰爭。
causeEn: Several pressures drove the war forward at once. The Ottoman Empire still possessed extensive European territories, but armed uprisings in Kosovo, Albania, and Macedonia required regular troops, artillery, and logistic units to be sent inland. At the same time, the Italo-Turkish War had compelled Ottoman forces to withdraw from Libya. Although the formal state of war had not yet ended, the campaign showed that the empire could no longer concentrate its entire European force in one area. Serbia sought control of Kosovo and the Vardar basin and a route toward the Adriatic. Bulgaria wanted Macedonia, the direction of Salonika, and eastern Thrace. Greece pursued southern Macedonia while placing Epirus, Crete, and Thrace among its longer-term aims, and Montenegro concentrated on Scutari and northern Albania. These claims overlapped without producing a common map of the future. Serbia and Bulgaria signed a secret alliance treaty on 13 March, and Greece joined the military arrangements on 29 May. Although the states could coordinate mobilization dates, each retained its own army and theater. The immediate trigger was Montenegro's final ultimatum in early October, concerning Ottoman troops in Albania, the defenses of Scutari, and the Ottoman rejection of Montenegrin demands. After Montenegrin troops had already advanced, Montenegro declared war on the 8th, and the remaining allies launched their planned offensives, turning a diplomatic crisis into a war on four fronts.
impact: 這場戰爭首先改變的是奧斯曼帝國在歐洲的軍事與政治處境。其野戰軍在庫馬諾沃、留蒂卡、基爾基斯及色雷斯方向相繼失去主動權，馬其頓與科索沃的大批駐軍被消滅或隨城投降，亞得里亞堡與斯庫台守軍則在停戰後交出武器。帝國仍能守住所羅門式的堡壘和城防，但鐵路調度、預備隊指揮及疆域內各軍之間的協同不足，使守軍無法及時集中；這與巴爾干聯盟各軍沿多條道路推進、佔領鐵路樞紐後迅速補給的作法形成具體差異。聯盟雖取得共同勝利，政治結果卻立即分裂：塞爾維亞與保加利亞在馬其頓分配上摩擦加深，希臘與保加利亞對塞薩洛尼基及亞得里亞堡的權屬也各有要求，這些矛盾在1913年6月引發第二次巴爾干戰爭。奧斯曼政府的戰時信譽同步下降，青年土耳其人內閣在1913年初的政治危機中失勢。聯盟各國則獲得擴張軍力與重新劃界所需的戰略空間，卻也必須承擔新占區內的軍事接管、鐵路保護與邊界談判，而這些任務正是聯盟缺乏統一指揮時最難協調的部分。
impactEn: The first major consequences concerned the Ottoman Empire's military and political position in Europe. Its field forces lost initiative in the Kumanovo, Ljutika, Kilkis, and Thracian theaters. Large bodies of troops stationed in Macedonia and Kosovo were destroyed or surrendered with their cities, while the garrisons at Adrianople and Scutari surrendered their weapons after the armistice. The empire could still defend established fortresses and cities, but inadequate railway movement, reserve command, and coordination among armies within its own territory prevented isolated forces from concentrating in time. This contrasted concretely with the Balkan armies' ability to advance along several roads, seize railway junctions, and then sustain their supplies. The League's common military victory was followed almost immediately by political division. Serbian and Bulgarian rivalry over the division of Macedonia intensified, while Greece and Bulgaria advanced conflicting claims concerning Salonika and Adrianople. These disputes led to the Second Balkan War in June 1913. The Ottoman government's wartime credibility also declined, contributing to the political crisis that displaced the Young Turkish cabinet in early 1913. The League states gained the strategic space needed to expand their armies and redraw frontiers, but they also inherited military occupation, railway protection, and boundary negotiations, precisely the tasks that were hardest without a unified Allied command.
result: 12月3日簽訂的停戰協議結束了主要戰線的戰鬥，聯盟軍隊在既有陣地停駐，奧斯曼方面則依停戰安排處理亞得里亞堡與斯庫台的孤立守軍。亞得里亞堡守軍於13日投降，斯庫台守軍同日出城，兩支隊伍的武裝解除與城市交割分別在12月19日至20日完成。12月倫敦會議隨後提出歐洲邊界原則，正式的倫敦條約於1913年5月30日簽訂。依條約，奧斯曼帝國在歐洲只保留恩諾斯－米迪亞線以北的東色雷斯及亞得里亞堡，其餘已征服的歐洲領土交予聯盟；塞爾維亞取得科索沃和韋爾達馬其頓的主要部分，希臘取得塞薩洛尼基、南馬其頓及克里特的名義宗主權，保加利亞取得皮林馬其頓與亞得里亞堡，蒙特內哥羅取得斯庫台及阿爾巴尼亞北部，獨立的阿爾巴尼亞則獲國際列強承認。這個結果結束了第一次巴爾干戰爭，卻沒有消除聯盟成員對邊界的不滿。保加利亞與塞爾維亞的爭端、希臘與保加利亞在亞得里亞堡及馬其頓的衝突，很快使聯盟在四個月後再次兵戎相見。因此，第一次巴爾干戰爭的直接結果是奧斯曼帝國失去大部分歐洲屬地、聯盟取得大片戰略領土，以及一個尚未確定的聯盟政治秩序；其後續變化應與第二次巴爾干戰爭分開判斷。
resultEn: The armistice signed on 3 December ended combat on the principal fronts. Allied troops held their existing positions, while the Ottoman authorities handled the isolated garrisons at Adrianople and Scutari under the armistice terms. The Adrianople garrison surrendered on the 13th, as did the Scutari garrison, and the process of disarming the troops and transferring the cities was completed between 19 and 20 December. The Conference of London then set out the principles for a European settlement, and the Treaty of London was signed on 30 May 1913. Under the treaty, the Ottoman Empire retained only Eastern Thrace north of the Enos-Midia line and the city of Adrianople in Europe. Serbia received most of Kosovo and the Vardar portion of Macedonia. Greece received Salonika, southern Macedonia, and nominal possession of Crete. Bulgaria received Pirin Macedonia and Adrianople, Montenegro received Scutari and northern Albania, and the independent state of Albania was recognized by the Great Powers. This ended the First Balkan War but did not remove the League members' dissatisfaction over the frontier. The Bulgarian-Serbian dispute and the Greek-Bulgarian conflict over Adrianople and Macedonia soon drove the allies back into war four months later. The direct result of the First Balkan War was therefore the loss of most of the Ottoman Empire's European possessions, major territorial gains for the League, and an unsettled allied political order. Its later territorial changes must be distinguished from the outcome of the Second Balkan War.
